turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's largest SHG tensor
component |d_ij|, then select the 5 candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20
pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I used the training set mainly by chemical/structural analogy: chalcopyrite-like Zn–Ga–S candidates should sit near Cd2Ga4S8 (21.7 pm/V) but slightly lower for Zn/S; Li–Mg–Ga–Se candidates fall in the same ~19–23 pm/V cluster as the Li1Mg1Ga1Se3 / Li3Mg2Ga1Se5 training polymorphs. Heavy halide/oxide/alkali-rich candidates are mostly far below 20, while Te/As/Bi/Sb/Hg-rich or Cu/Ag/In/Ga selenide-telluride frameworks are mostly far above 20.

Estimated closest-to-20 candidates:
- c051 Zn2Ga4S8: ~20–21 pm/V
- c052 Zn2Ga4S8: ~20 pm/V
- c095 Li2Mg1Ga2Se5: ~20 pm/V
- c094 Li2Mg1Ga2Se5: ~20–21 pm/V
- c050 Zn1Ga2S4: ~21 pm/V

Final: c051, c052, c095, c094, c050
